perf.summary: BFS 'pop front' shifts the entire stack array left by one every iteration, making the traversal O(n^2) in queue length.
perf.currentCost: Lines 256-261: after reading regs[stack[0]] it does nStack-- then a loop copying stack[j]=stack[j+1] for all remaining entries. Each pop is O(nStack); total work for the layer-build traversal is quadratic in the number of regions pushed (up to maxStack=64 per root, repeated per root).
perf.proposedChange: Replace the front-shift queue with a head/tail ring or a head index: keep 'int head=0' and 'int nStack', pop via 'var reg=&regs[stack[head++]];' and push at tail; the buffer holds at most maxStack live entries (size it accordingly or wrap). This turns each pop into O(1).
perf.rationale: Eliminates the O(n) memmove per pop, reducing the BFS from O(n^2) to O(n) in entries processed. For dense layered heightfields where regions count is high this is a real asymptotic win on a build-time path.
perf.risk: Must preserve FIFO order (original pops index 0, i.e. front) so layer assignment order is unchanged; a head-index queue preserves FIFO exactly. Ensure backing buffer capacity accounts for head advancing (use a separate ring or only push while nStack<maxStack as today, tracking live count = tail-head). Behavior identical.
